**SEC-10 · `plugins/flow/agents/code-reviewer.md:147`**
Cycle 1 fixed the plugin-root resolver inside the script and then added a **caller** using the old one, whose first candidate is a working-directory-relative `plugins/flow` — and during a review the working directory is the repository under review. Demonstrated: a branch shipping `plugins/flow/bin/flow-clone-scan.sh` had its own scanner executed, printing a forged `STATE=none`. `references/plugin-root-resolution.md` records that `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` is unset for an agent's Bash step, so this was the normal case. _(HIGH · unchallenged)_

**SEC-9 · `plugins/flow/bin/flow-clone-scan.sh:378`**
Cycle 1's ReDoS fix covered one shape. Runs of `**/` collapse; a run of `**` not followed by a slash does not, and counts as one group each — so `****************ZZZ` sits exactly at the eight-group bound. Measured 13.4 s for a single path, and across the tree it pinned a core for 300 s producing no output at all. _(HIGH · unchallenged)_

**C2-F1 · `plugins/flow/bin/flow-clone-scan.sh:213`**
Cycle 1 changed the exclude delimiter from comma to newline; `cascade-resolve.sh` refuses any resolved value containing a control character, and `_resolve` swallowed the warning. Every project's `excludePaths` was discarded in complete silence and the built-in list used instead. One entry passes trivially, which is why nothing caught it. _(HIGH · unchallenged)_

**C2-F2 · `plugins/flow/bin/flow-clone-scan.sh:171`**
`SETTINGS_SOURCE`, added in cycle 1 to make provenance visible, could not tell "the cascade answered" from "the cascade handed back my default" — it exits 0 with the default. Two runs applying different thresholds were identical on the line meant to separate them. _(HIGH · unchallenged)_

**ERR-12 · `plugins/flow/bin/flow-clone-scan.sh:183`**

F1 | correctness | `log-commits.sh` | Exited 1 on a repository with no `.decisions/` directory: a failing subshell under `set -e` aborted the hook where the surrounding code intended to skip.

F2 | correctness | `journal-read-section.sh` | Hung forever on a flag with no value. `shift 2` with one argument left returns non-zero but leaves `$1` in place, and the file has no `set -e`, so the argument loop never advanced. Confirmed still spinning after 3s.
F3 | correctness | `flow-strip-auto-log.sh` | Dry-run and apply could disagree on a CRLF journal: the locked reader decodes universal newlines, so the write converted every line ending in the file.
F4 | docs | `flow-strip-auto-log.sh` | The header did not state that a rewritten file gains a trailing newline, nor what happens to CRLF.

F5 | correctness | `flow-strip-auto-log.sh` | A fence closed whenever the character appeared, so a 4-backtick block closed at its first inner 3-backtick line and a breadcrumb quoted below it was deleted. The writer and reader had the same rule; the reader's was weaker still (`index(line, char)`).

F6 | test-coverage | `flow-strip-auto-log.test.sh` | The blank-line pairing tests each had a single blank, so a version that collapsed a run passed them. Separately, the strip commit is not byte-reproducible by the current script in 2 of 28 files.
F7 | test-coverage | `journal-append.test.sh` | Nothing pinned the heading match as exact rather than a prefix.

F8 | test-coverage | `auto-log-relocation.test.sh` | Nothing asserted that the out-of-repo early return still reaches the quality-ledger block, which depends on every guard being `return 0` and not `exit 0`.
F9 | correctness | `_journal_atomic.py` | An unclosed fence in the section being replaced ran the skip loop to EOF, deleting the heading it swallowed and every section after it — silently.
F10 | correctness | `journal-append.sh` | A dangling flag aborted with exit 1 and no diagnostic, and an empty `--replace-heading` was accepted as "append".
F11 | correctness | `journal-read-section.sh` | The reader returned both copies of a duplicated heading while the writer replaces only the first — the two disagreeing about what the section is.
F12 | security | `log-commits.sh` | Three diagnostics echoed a journal path without `one_line()`, so a filename containing a newline could forge a second report line.

F13 | docs | `commands/setup.md` | Nothing told `/flow:setup` to surface `STRIP_AUTO_LOG_WARN`, which can appear with `0 files, 0 lines` — so an operator shown only the counts would learn nothing about the journal that needs a manual look.

**SEC1 · `plugins/dossier/tests/hooks.test.sh:657`**

**SEC2 · `plugins/dossier/tests/hooks.test.sh:649`**

**ERR2 · `plugins/dossier/tests/hooks.test.sh:649`**

**ERR3 · `plugins/dossier/tests/hooks.test.sh:667`**

**ERR4 · `plugins/dossier/tests/run.sh:110`**
